newsitem.title: UK: Study sees growth for Europe long-term insurance.
newsitem.headline: Study sees growth for Europe long-term insurance.

text.p: Strong growth will occur in the European long-term insurance market, according to a report from analysts Datamonitor.
The report predicts European life and pensions markets will grow at an average of 13.3 per cent between 1996 and 2002, when it will be worth $608,514 million.
France and Germany will continue to lead the market, accounting for 26.1 per cent and 18.5 per cent respectively in 2002, with the UK in third place with 13.7 per cent.

The Portuguese market grew fastest between 1991 and 1996, with an average premium growth rate of 36.2 per cent in real terms. Greece also saw strong growth, although it was heavily affected by inflation.
"Individuals are becoming increasingly aware of the need to provide for their own future as most governments face growing economic and social problems," said report author Maria Franco.
"Countries such as Portugal and Greece offer great opportunities for insurers who wish to expand their operations world-wide," she said.
